newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico stocks roar on Dow Coattails.
newsitem.headline: Mexico stocks roar on Dow Coattails.

text.p: Mexican stocks notched up sharp gains to close near an all-time record on Monday after an all-time high on Wall Street lured foreign investors and kept the bulls charging on the bourse, dealers said.
The leading IPC share index ended up 56.71 points, or 1.46 percent, at 3,930.09. The Dow Jones Industrial Average soared 123.22 points to close at a record 7,292.75.
"Now today really was interesting, for several reasons, including upside carried over from last week on technicals, the Dow (Jones) and foreigners stepping in," a trader said.
Dealers said the bourse had been in a lull since the IPC set its closing record of 3,938.69 points on February 25.
Hector Jimenez, an analyst at the Inverlat brokerage said telecomms stock Telmex lead the rally, which was also driven by foreign buyers.
"Foreigners were a little more active, some stocks had lagged far behind the market and Telmex also had an impact after its ADR broke resistance at 42-1/2," he said.

Telmex ADRs closed up 1-5/8 at 43-3/4, while their L shares rose 54 centavos to a record close in peso terms of 17.34. Dealers said Telmex ADRs were still substantially below 1994 levels, however, when they had traded at more than $70.
Dealers said foreign buying raised trading volume to a brisk 98.9 million shares.
"The market is waking up at last, but could could slow down once it rises above 3,960 points," a dealer said.
On the broad market, of 115 stocks traded, gains outpaced losses by 62 to 30.
Tourist company Situr headed the percentage gainers' list, up six centavos at 42 centavos, followed by its debt-ridden holding company Sidek, which gained five centavos to 53 centavos.
Situr announced during the session that one of its subsidiaries had extended maturity on its medium-term promissory notes.
"Sidek gained on nickel-and-dime dealing, out of sheer speculation over a debt-restructuring deal," a trader said.
